name: refactor_terraform_per_env_variables_to_map
description: Collapses three copy-pasted per-environment string variables (each with an identical allowlist validation block) into one map(string) variable with a single validation checking every value, proven by real terraform validate; behavior-drift broken swaps alltrue for anytrue, so only ONE environment's value needs to be valid for the whole map to pass
prompts: main.tf declares three separate string variables - dev_instance_type, staging_instance_type, prod_instance_type - each with its own default and an IDENTICAL validation block checking the value is one of t3.micro/t3.small/t3.medium. Consolidate these into a single variable named instance_types of type map(string), keyed by environment (dev, staging, prod) with the same three defaults, and ONE validation block whose condition checks that EVERY value in the map is in the allowed list (not just one of them). Remove the three old variables entirely. Run `terraform fmt`.

test_setup_files.check_instance_types.py:
import json
import subprocess

def run(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)

fmt = run(["terraform", "fmt", "-check", "-diff"])
assert fmt.returncode == 0, f"terraform fmt -check failed:\n{fmt.stdout}\n{fmt.stderr}"

init = run(["terraform", "init", "-backend=false", "-input=false"])
assert init.returncode == 0, f"terraform init failed:\n{init.stdout}\n{init.stderr}"

validate = run(["terraform", "validate", "-no-color", "-json"])
data = json.loads(validate.stdout)
assert data.get("valid") is True, f"terraform validate failed on the valid defaults: {validate.stdout}\n{validate.stderr}"

# terraform validate only checks static syntax/types - custom `validation`
# blocks are evaluated during planning, so use `terraform plan` (no actual
# resources reference the variable, so this never touches real
# infrastructure or the network) to prove the rule really fires.
plan_good = run(["terraform", "plan", "-input=false", "-no-color"])
assert plan_good.returncode == 0, (
    f"terraform plan failed on the valid defaults (it shouldn't have):\n"
    f"{plan_good.stdout}\n{plan_good.stderr}")

content = open("main.tf", encoding="utf-8").read()
assert content.count('variable "instance_types"') == 1, (
    "expected ONE consolidated instance_types variable, not three separate per-environment variables")
assert 'variable "dev_instance_type"' not in content, "the old per-environment variables should be removed"
assert 'variable "staging_instance_type"' not in content, "the old per-environment variables should be removed"
assert 'variable "prod_instance_type"' not in content, "the old per-environment variables should be removed"

# Corrupt ONLY the prod default (the first occurrence of "t3.medium" in the
# file - the map default comes before the validation block's allowlist) to
# an out-of-allowlist value, and confirm the validation rule actually
# rejects it during planning - proving every map value is checked, not
# just one.
bad_content = content.replace('"t3.medium"', '"m5.xlarge"', 1)
assert bad_content != content, "could not locate the prod default value to corrupt for the negative test"
open("main.tf", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(bad_content)

plan_bad = run(["terraform", "plan", "-input=false", "-no-color"])
assert plan_bad.returncode != 0, (
    "terraform plan should REJECT an out-of-allowlist instance type in ANY environment, but it "
    "succeeded - the validation condition must check ALL map values, not just one of them")
assert "must be one of" in plan_bad.stdout + plan_bad.stderr, (
    f"plan failed, but not for the expected validation reason:\n{plan_bad.stdout}\n{plan_bad.stderr}")

print("PASS terraform consolidated-variable validation checks")
